synopsis: Mevea is a commercial Lappeenranta University spin-off founded in 2005, positioned for mobile machinery across construction, mining, ports, forestry and tractor research [f8560, f9100, f8667]. Its vendor-described capabilities include real-time multibody dynamics, hydraulics, powertrain, sensors, HIL I/O and dynamic soil interaction with buckets, tracks and tires; however, the booklet assesses heavy-machine physics tools as having thin sensor and scenario tooling and explicitly labels Mevea's sensor capabilities as vendor claims [f8561, f8283, f9102]. Documented applications include Siemens SIMOCRANE crane-automation twins in 2023, an academic tractor digital twin with CAN control in 2026, and mining training simulators; Mevea claims over 100 simulator models supplied to more than 50 customers [f8564, f8565, f8567, f8563]. Simulink co-simulation through FMI or TCP/IP is explicitly supported, and the example middle- and highest-cost chains use Mevea for terrain, hydraulics, machine variants or heavy-machine dynamics [f8562, f8699, f9286, f9304]. Its October 2026 seminar covers verification and validation cases from Prinoth, Oamk and IAAPS, while human-in-the-loop simulators such as Mevea may be needed for warning-then-brake human factors; public pricing and the latest release were not found [f8566, f9379, f9104, f9105].
